q1_mapped.layout: row, beer, beer_id, tasting_category_fine, chem__<231 x 1.csv columns>, <50 target columns in targetcolumns.csv order>

q2_raw.layout: same as q1_mapped, but the 50 target columns keep the 4.csv standardized values

targetColumnsCheck.verdict: 50/50 target columns present in 4.csv with the exact declared names; 4.csv carries exactly 3 metadata columns + the 50 declared targets and nothing else.

rowAlignment.beerOrderNote: beer is a permutation of 1..250 (same permutation in 1.csv, 4.csv and 8.xlsx), NOT the row number: row 0 has beer=10, row 1 has beer=86. So "row 3" and "beer 3" are different samples; always use row (the positional id) for the split and report the beer value alongside it.
rowAlignment.joinPolicy: row position 0..249 of 4.csv; beer would also be legal (identical permutation, unique) but beer_id is truncated. No sort, no filter, no drop before assigning row.

beerIdTruncation.verdict: 4.csv (and 7.csv) beer_id is numerically truncated: 250 rows collapse to only 96 distinct values, and one 4.csv beer_id covers up to 20 different beers. beer_id is therefore NEVER a join key; every cross-table merge uses the 0-based row position, which is proven safe by the beer/tasting_category_fine cell-by-cell equality below.

scaleAudit.rule: A column can be one of three things and they are NOT interchangeable: (1) log10-transformed concentration, (2) raw concentration, (3) zero-floor-coded log10. Evidence per column: exact numeric identity with 8.xlsx Calibrated raw concentrations under each hypothesis for the 70 columns that appear there; otherwise the sign of the values (raw concentrations cannot be negative) plus column-family coherence. No column was assumed: the classification is computed in this script and stored per column below.

missingHandling.policy: Explicit rule, train statistics only. For every chemical/physical column with missing cells, NaN is replaced by the MEDIAN of that column over the 200 TRAIN rows of the seed-20261024 holdout (the same rows split.py will assign). Test-row values are never used to compute an imputed value; the test median is recorded as a diagnostic only. No target column has a missing value (4.csv is complete), so imputation never touches the Q1/Q2 labels and cannot leak into zmin/zmax.
missingHandling.q3Note: Q3 reuses the same 250-row, same-seed positional split, so these train-row medians are also the correct imputation statistics for q3_table.csv.

mappedGrade.zSource: 4.csv target column, unchanged (standardized/centred continuous value, not original 0-6)

outOfRangeCounts.toleranceNote: A cell counts as out of range only when it is more than 1e-09 outside the interval. The strict counts (also recorded per target as nMappedBelow0Strict / nMappedAbove6Strict) add cells that sit on the boundary and differ from it by last-bit float noise; those are not real violations.
outOfRangeCounts.reason: Train rows map exactly into [0,6] by construction (zmin->0, zmax->6). Test rows whose z falls outside the TRAIN z-range map outside [0,6]; the values are kept un-clipped so the evaluation sees the true linear map instead of a silently saturated label.

mappedGrade.constantColumnPolicy: If zmax == zmin on the train rows the linear map is undefined; the script then writes 3.0 (the 0-6 midpoint) for every row of that target and flags it in perTarget.constantColumn. This dataset has 0 such column(s) (none).

zGlobal.note: 4.csv is a standardized value, so z is not bounded by 0..6: clove reaches z=6.17 on the train rows (and 6.172383248 overall). This is the direct proof that the 4.csv numbers are not original 0-6 panel scores.

extremes.note: Both extremes are TEST rows whose z lies outside the train z-range; train rows stay inside [0,6] by construction.

roundTripCheck.purpose: proves that the chem__ columns carry the 1.csv values bit-for-bit (only the imputed cells differ) and that the target blocks survived the CSV write, instead of trusting that it did.
roundTripCheck.pandasFloatParserNote: pandas' default C parser can land 1 ULP (2.2e-16) away from a 17-significant-digit decimal; that is why the mapped grade is written with 12 digits, which round-trips exactly. 4.csv's own values are short enough decimals that they round-trip as they are, so q2_raw keeps them bit-identical.
roundTripCheck.verdict: PASS: every non-missing chem__ cell is bit-identical to 1.csv, no cell was written as NaN, the Q2 target block is bit-identical to 4.csv, and the Q1 target block equals the computed mapped grade rounded to 12 significant digits

defectThresholdPolicy.decidedAt: data layer (data-engineer), before any Q3 modelling
defectThresholdPolicy.rule: A compound is a DEFECT constraint only if (a) the problem statement names it among the defect compounds OR 8.xlsx carries an off_flavors marker for it, AND (b) 8.xlsx carries a real numeric threshold for it. Thresholds that merely describe a typical/detection level (bitterness 5 IBU, ethanol 1.76 %v/v, protein 1.02 g/L ...) are REFERENCE levels: they stay in the dataset as thr__ columns but must never be used to declare a defect.

defectSet.label: DMS
defectSet.offFlavors: cooked vegetables, onion, garlic, corn, black currant, sulfidic, cabbage, tinned tomato, baked beans

defectCompoundsNotEvaluable.label: trans-2-nonenal
defectCompoundsNotEvaluable.reason: the compound exists in the sheet AND in 1.csv (X.E..2.nonenal), but the sheet has no numeric threshold for it: the defect constraint is NOT evaluable from this attachment and no value is invented.

defectCompoundsNotEvaluable.label: Stale hops
defectCompoundsNotEvaluable.reason: "stale hops" is not a compound row of the 'Sensory thresholds' sheet at all: in this dataset it is a SENSORY descriptor (4.csv target "stale_hops", 7.csv descriptors), so there is no concentration and no threshold to compare.

defectThresholdPolicy.consequence: Q3 must evaluate defect constraints only on defectSetColumns (each with its real unit and its log10/raw scale from scaleAudit), and must report trans-2-nonenal and "stale hops" as limitations rather than inventing thresholds for them.

calibratedCrossCheck.purpose: 8.xlsx "Calibrated chemical dataset" is used ONLY to corroborate the per-column scale verdicts of 1.csv. It is never a model input, never a split source and never an imputation source.
calibratedCrossCheck.calibratedRowsWithValuesButNaN: the Calibrated sheet has NaN where 1.csv has a value (and vice versa) in a minority of cells; counted by nRowsCompared < 250 above
calibratedCrossCheck.verdict: 70/70 aligned columns reproduce 1.csv exactly under ONE single transform hypothesis (worst per-column median |diff| = 0, tolerance 1e-6); 73 cells in 30 columns disagree by more than 1e-3, and every one of them is a row-level blemish of the Calibrated sheet (e.g. row 105 / beer 177 for n.hexanol and Z.nerolidol), not a transform ambiguity. No column verdict depends on those cells.

notes: data/raw/* is never modified: every output is a NEW file under data/processed/.

Q1 targets are mapped grade only; the original 0-6 panel scores are not recoverable (3.xlsx scorecards are empty templates, 3.xlsx summary results are all zero, the 4.csv standardization parameters are unknown, and clove z > 6).
Q2 targets are the 4.csv standardized values unchanged; the file exists so Q2 can run its association analysis on a dataset that is explicitly NOT the mapped grade.
The chemical/physical columns are identical in q1_mapped.csv and q2_raw.csv so that the two datasets differ only in the 50 target columns.
5/6/7 (and 2.csv) are derived Spearman matrices of the same 250 samples; they are not independent external data and are not used in this preparation step.
